items.headline: Medetomidine withdrawal is driving ICU-level care
items.summary: At two Penn hospitals, use of dexmedetomidine among inpatients with opioid use disorder rose from about 6% to about 20% after mid-2024. It reached about 32% in the last quarter they looked at. Hospitalist, ED, and consult teams should plan for alpha-2 withdrawal protocols and ICU beds.

items.headline: NOHARM trial
items.summary: Six surgical centers built a nondrug pain pathway into the medical record. It cut in-hospital opioids and discharge prescriptions without worsening pain, function, or safety.

items.headline: One in nine older adult cannabis users meet criteria for cannabis use disorder
items.summary: That's 11.4% of past-year users aged 65 and up. Most cases are mild, but nearly a quarter are moderate or severe, which makes a case for screening in primary care and geriatrics.

items.headline: HRSA awarded $89.3M for rural addiction care
items.summary: The money comes through its Rural Communities Opioid Response Program and reaches 45 states and one territory. It's separate from Monday's $247.9M SAMHSA package.

items.headline: CDC report on buprenorphine access
items.summary: Rural pharmacy availability rose from 65% to 80%. Emergency departments starting patients on buprenorphine still lag, at about 10% in rural areas versus 31% in cities.
